findings.body: The view-only administrator passes `canManage()` and can perform group-management operations despite having no `manage` permission.
findings.failure_mode: Authorization decisions for global group mutations accept read-only permissions.
findings.impact: The view-only administrator passes `canManage()` and can perform group-management operations despite having no `manage` permission.
findings.root_cause: The V2 global group-management check treats the view scope as sufficient for management.
findings.suggested_fix: Check only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` in `canManage()`; retain `VIEW` as a valid scope only for `canView()`.
findings.title: View-only all-groups permission grants group management
findings.trigger: With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an administrator has only the `view` scope on the all-groups resource and calls an endpoint that invokes `requireManage()` for groups, such as creating a top-level group.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 70 verbatim shows `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` in `canManage()`. The method accepts VIEW scope for management authorization. Comparing to `canManage(GroupModel group)` at line 79 which correctly checks only MANAGE scope, and to the V1 `GroupPermissions.canManage()` at line 274-276 which only checks `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS`, this is an authorization bypass where VIEW-only permission grants management capability.

raw_findings.body: The view-only administrator passes `canManage()` and can perform group-management operations despite having no `manage` permission.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Authorization decisions for global group mutations accept read-only permissions.
raw_findings.impact: The view-only administrator passes `canManage()` and can perform group-management operations despite having no `manage` permission.
raw_findings.root_cause: The V2 global group-management check treats the view scope as sufficient for management.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Check only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` in `canManage()`; retain `VIEW` as a valid scope only for `canView()`.
raw_findings.title: View-only all-groups permission grants group management
raw_findings.trigger: With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an administrator has only the `view` scope on the all-groups resource and calls an endpoint that invokes `requireManage()` for groups, such as creating a top-level group.

raw_findings.body: The enumeration returns no group resources, so `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set and authorized group members are omitted from group-filtered counts and queries.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The permission-to-group-ID projection silently produces no entries even when per-group policies grant access.
raw_findings.impact: The enumeration returns no group resources, so `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set and authorized group members are omitted from group-filtered counts and queries.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new V2 lookup requires a resource type that the schema resource-creation path does not set for group-specific resources.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Assign `AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE` to each schema-created group resource, or enumerate the schema's group resources using a predicate that matches their actual persisted representation.
raw_findings.title: Group permission enumeration searches for an unset resource type
raw_findings.trigger: A per-group `VIEW_MEMBERS` or `MANAGE_MEMBERS` policy is created through the V2 schema, whose group-specific resources are created without assigning the `Groups` type, and a user count or filtered user query requests group-scoped results.

raw_findings.body: `hasPermission` cannot find the specific resource because it looks up the supplied value by name, so valid per-group permissions are ignored and the group is not returned.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Per-group access is lost during the conversion from authorization resources to user-query group filters.
raw_findings.impact: `hasPermission` cannot find the specific resource because it looks up the supplied value by name, so valid per-group permissions are ignored and the group is not returned.
raw_findings.root_cause: The callback confuses the authorization resource's internal database ID with the group identifier expected by `hasPermission`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the group resource name (the schema stores the group model ID as the resource name), or add a helper that evaluates the already-fetched `groupResource` directly.
raw_findings.title: Per-group permission checks pass the authorization resource ID as a group ID
raw_findings.trigger: The resource enumeration reaches a group-specific resource and the administrator has a member-view permission on that group, but the authorization resource's internal ID differs from the group resource name/group model ID.

raw_findings.body: User storage compares memberships against group model IDs, so the authorization resource IDs do not match and authorized users are excluded from filtered searches and counts.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Authorized users disappear from group-scoped result sets even after the permission has been correctly evaluated.
raw_findings.impact: User storage compares memberships against group model IDs, so the authorization resource IDs do not match and authorized users are excluded from filtered searches and counts.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new projection emits authorization-resource identifiers where downstream user queries require realm group identifiers.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add the group model ID stored in the resource name, for example `groupResource.getName()`, rather than the authorization resource's internal ID.
raw_findings.title: Group-filter IDs use authorization resource IDs instead of group model IDs
raw_findings.trigger: A group resource is accepted by the permission check and the resulting set is passed to `UsersResource`/the user provider as the `groupIds` filter.

finding.verifier_reason: The claim that group resources are created without GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE is unsubstantiated. AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource at lines 121-127 shows resources are created with scopes from getResourceTypes().get(resourceType), and the schema defines GROUPS with GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE. The candidate speculates about resource creation behavior not evidenced in the patch or context.

finding.body: `hasPermission` cannot find the specific resource because it looks up the supplied value by name, so valid per-group permissions are ignored and the group is not returned.
finding.failure_mode: Per-group access is lost during the conversion from authorization resources to user-query group filters.

finding.root_cause: The callback confuses the authorization resource's internal database ID with the group identifier expected by `hasPermission`.
finding.suggested_fix: Pass the group resource name (the schema stores the group model ID as the resource name), or add a helper that evaluates the already-fetched `groupResource` directly.
finding.title: Per-group permission checks pass the authorization resource ID as a group ID
finding.trigger: The resource enumeration reaches a group-specific resource and the administrator has a member-view permission on that group, but the authorization resource's internal ID differs from the group resource name/group model ID.
finding.verifier_reason: Line 122 shows `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` where groupResource.getId() is the authorization Resource's internal ID. However, hasPermission at line 141 does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` - it looks up by name, not by ID. AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup at line 185 returns `group.getId()` as the resource name. So passing the Resource's internal ID to hasPermission will fail the lookup since it expects the group model ID (which is stored as resource name).

finding.body: User storage compares memberships against group model IDs, so the authorization resource IDs do not match and authorized users are excluded from filtered searches and counts.
finding.failure_mode: Authorized users disappear from group-scoped result sets even after the permission has been correctly evaluated.
finding.impact: User storage compares memberships against group model IDs, so the authorization resource IDs do not match and authorized users are excluded from filtered searches and counts.
finding.root_cause: The new projection emits authorization-resource identifiers where downstream user queries require realm group identifiers.
finding.suggested_fix: Add the group model ID stored in the resource name, for example `groupResource.getName()`, rather than the authorization resource's internal ID.
finding.title: Group-filter IDs use authorization resource IDs instead of group model IDs
finding.trigger: A group resource is accepted by the permission check and the resulting set is passed to `UsersResource`/the user provider as the `groupIds` filter.
finding.verifier_reason: Line 123 `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the authorization Resource's internal ID, but downstream user queries expect group model IDs. This is the same root cause as candidate 2 - confusion between authorization resource ID and group model ID. The fix would be the same: use groupResource.getName() which contains the group model ID per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup.
